title: New Orleans roots, teaching lineage, and a workshop for street players
summary: He says New Orleans musicians descend from the originators, names the teacher lineage through Alvin Batiste to Wes Anderson, and hopes for a workshop for raw young talent.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: to explore some of these things. But when you come from New Orleans, you're a branch off the original tree. This is where it started. So it's like being a direct descendant of Sidney Bechet or Louis Cottrell or Willie Humphrey and on and on and on the great people that came afterwards. I learned from Alvin Baptiste and Wes Anderson learned from Alvin Baptiste and I taught Wes. And we all somehow wind up teaching each other either something of music or a life of spirituality or just sharing our lives together. Those roots go very, very deep and we're all entangled and entwined and all for positive, forceful good. I mean, I don't think that there's... Anytime I see any one of us in the musical community that we have here make great strides or from collaborations that I've had or things that they've passed on, I'm always happy to see the other successes that come. And I'm just happy that myself and David and all the rest of us have had a chance to put our hearts and souls into some projects and to see that it's an ongoing music and I know that it will never fade out or die because you see all these new things that's happening. One of the other things I always thought about the workshop is that to play the kind of music that the extended forms of jazz or from bebop and beyond or the newer music, you need great technical facility and I would also hope that some of the young musicians that we see that have tremendous talent that are somewhat playing raw on the streets and not getting the very direct private lessons and musical lessons that allow them to take their talents even further that we sort of develop this raw talent that we see playing on the streets and somehow form a workshop or places that they can go to not only play the music they play but get individual development and instruction and compositional guidance, theoretical guidance so that they can be the very best that they can be.
